name: Ambala–Narnaul Expressway

tollInfo.note: This road is tolled. Indian toll rates are revised every year on 1 April, so check the current notification before you travel.

timeline.event: Taken up under the Bharatmala programme as the Ambala–Kotputli economic corridor

history: NH 152D is a brand-new expressway that cuts diagonally across Haryana, from Ismailabad near Ambala in the north to Narnaul in the south. It was taken up under the Bharatmala programme as part of the longer Ambala–Kotputli corridor, and because it was built on completely fresh ground away from towns, drivers can cross almost the whole state without passing through a single city. Building it meant buying land from farmers across about 112 villages in eight districts, and the road was finished in roughly three years. It opened on 1 August 2022 and is now the quickest way from Chandigarh and Ambala towards Jaipur, skipping Delhi completely. At Narnaul the route carries on as NH 148B to Paniyala Mod near Kotputli on the Delhi–Jaipur highway.
facts: Known as the Trans-Haryana Expressway; built as a greenfield road across eight districts.
Cuts several hours off the drive from Ambala towards Jaipur by avoiding Delhi.
At Narnaul it links onward towards Kotputli, forming the Ambala–Kotputli corridor.
Built under the Bharatmala programme by NHAI.
Has about 16 interchanges along its 227 km — otherwise it is fully access-controlled.
Passes through the districts of Ambala, Kurukshetra, Kaithal, Jind, Rohtak, Bhiwani, Charkhi Dadri and Mahendragarh.
Because it was built away from every town, there is not a single traffic light on the whole road.
significance: Traffic heading from Punjab, Himachal Pradesh and Jammu towards Rajasthan and Gujarat used to have to squeeze past Delhi. This expressway lets it slice straight down the middle of Haryana instead, taking trucks and cars out of the capital's jams and pollution. It has also opened up the dry southern districts of Haryana — Jind, Charkhi Dadri, Mahendragarh — which had no fast road of their own.

travelNotes: Ambala to Narnaul takes roughly three and a half to four hours with almost nothing to slow you down. The flip side of a greenfield road is that there is very little beside it — plan your fuel and food stops, because petrol pumps and dhabas are far apart and there is not much lighting at night. Thick fog in December and January can cut visibility badly on this open, flat stretch, so it is worth checking conditions before an early winter start.
futureUpgrades: NHAI has taken up a greenfield link of about 86 km from the Narnaul/Paniyala end to the Delhi–Mumbai Expressway near Barodameo in Alwar district, so northern states get a direct run onto that expressway.
